## Summary

`local_max_concurrent_queries: 1` in `proxy/config.yaml` is legacy dead config: the router derives the local concurrency limit from `session_slot_pool_size` (currently 3) in `router._get_local_max_concurrent_queries()`, with the legacy key only as a backward-compat fallback defaulting to 1. An operator reading the config sees a concurrency limit of 1 that is never applied, which is misleading (the effective limit is 3 slots). Discovered during the local-model busy-time analysis (LP-0MSG97N2F0090TO9).

The config comment already acknowledges the derivation ("This value is now derived from session_slot_pool_size by default... preserved for explicit override only") — the ambiguity is that the key still exists and can silently override pool size if set.

## User Story

As an operator, I want exactly one config key to control local concurrency, so that I cannot be misled by a dead/misleading setting.

## Expected behaviour / outcomes

- `session_slot_pool_size` is the single, documented source of truth for local concurrency.
- The legacy `local_max_concurrent_queries` key and its fallback path in `router._get_local_max_concurrent_queries()` are removed, OR (if removal is deemed too risky) the key is commented out with a clear deprecation note and the fallback path logs a warning when used.
- No behavioural change in normal operation (concurrency stays 3).

## Suggested approach

1. Remove `local_max_concurrent_queries: 1` from `proxy/config.yaml` and simplify the surrounding comment.
2. Update `router._get_local_max_concurrent_queries()` to read only `session_slot_pool_size` (drop the legacy fallback), or keep the fallback but log a deprecation warning.
3. Run proxy tests; verify no config-validation tests reference the key (see also config-consistency validation LP-0MSCABA5K0010LW2).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No reference to `local_max_concurrent_queries` remains in config or code (or, if kept as fallback, it logs a deprecation warning and is commented out in config).
- [ ] Proxy test suite passes; concurrency behaviour unchanged (limit = `session_slot_pool_size` = 3).
- [ ] Config comment updated to state `session_slot_pool_size` is the single source of truth.
data.title: Remove dead local_max_concurrent_queries config; session_slot_pool_size is the single source of truth

data.description:
# Bump local slot-exhaustion retry attempts 1 -> 2

## Problem statement

Recommendation from the 2026-08-11 proxy usage analysis (maximize local LLM utilization). `local_slot_exhaustion_retry_attempts: 1` with `local_slot_exhaustion_retry_delay_seconds: 0.1` gives a single grace retry before a request falls back to the remote tier when the local probe reports 0 available slots. Its documented purpose is right-after-restart races where slot probes briefly report 0 available. Bumping to 2 retries catches the same race plus near-finished streams that free a slot within ~0.2s.

Expected effect is sub-1% of fallbacks (contention fallbacks are 839/1608 = 52%, but the large majority are genuinely long streams, not sub-200ms races — see the cheap-mode queue policy item for the real contention lever). Low risk: adds at most ~0.2s latency to the remote-fallback path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `local_slot_exhaustion_retry_attempts` set to 2 (delay 0.1s unchanged).
2. Routing logic unchanged otherwise: still falls back to the next provider after the retries are exhausted.
3. Tests: right-after-restart probe race resolves to local on the second retry; persistent exhaustion still falls back after 2 retries; total added latency bounded (~0.2s + probe time).
4. Full test suite passes (quiet mode).
data.title: Bump local_slot_exhaustion_retry_attempts 1 -> 2 (grace retry on slot exhaustion)

# Feature: Proxy-side proactive session compaction (Tier 1)

**STATUS: DEFERRED — implementation delayed until client-side compaction
results are available.** Client-side compaction machinery is now in place in
ContextHub (Compact-and-Continue WL-0MR269PDV00970YP, auto-continue
WL-0MSMGGPWR000MZ0O; gate-response wiring WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6). Per
operator decision (2026-08-28), server-side compaction must not be
implemented until results from the client-side effort are reviewed; this
item is parked (status `blocked`) pending that review.

Implementation of the F4 recommendation (LP-0MTC8BWV50012WSW,
`docs/session-compaction-recommendations.md`) within the two-tier scheme of
LP-0MTCW79RR000LFMJ. The proxy compacts the session at **prompt-assembly
time** when estimated tokens exceed the trigger — no round trip, no
client-side coordination.

## Behavior (both modes — Strategy C, summarize-first)

Per operator decision (2026-08-28), serve-side compaction uses the hybrid
Strategy C in **both** fast and cheap modes, with the **first prompt always
retained verbatim**.

### Retention invariant (fast AND cheap)

The compacted prompt MUST always contain, unchanged:

1. the system prompt;
2. the **very first user prompt** (the original task statement/setup, which
   carries essential instructions);
3. the most recent turns within budget.

Everything between the first prompt and the recent window is folded into a
summary injected at the top of the prompt (below the retained first prompt).

### Fast mode — Strategy C

- **Trigger:** `estimated_tokens > 58,300` (= 0.70 × per-slot clamp 83,285).
  Fires before the existing `context_pressure_warn_ratio` (0.8 × 83,285 =
  66.6K) so compaction is proactive, not reactive.
- **Target:** compacted prompt ≤ 38,000 tokens (`local_large_context_cold_cache_threshold`,
  fast profile): retain system prompt + first prompt + recent turns; fold
  the rest into a summary.
- **Backstop:** only if the session still exceeds budget after summarizing,
  drop oldest non-first turns (whole turns, never splittable, never the
  system prompt or first prompt), logged.
- **Automatic** on breach.

### Cheap mode — Strategy C (hybrid)

- **Trigger:** `estimated_tokens > 43,000` (= 0.70 × static clamp 61,440).
- **Target:** compacted prompt ≤ 30,000 tokens: same retention invariant +
  summary of the middle.
- **Non-compactable** (summarizer unavailable, or still over budget after
  compaction): route remote with guidance — never silent remote fallback,
  never near-full-slot local prefill (LP-0MSORQVK50012Q4D AC4).
- **Automatic** on breach.

## Implementation approach

- **Trigger hook:** reuse the existing `context_pressure` machinery in
  `proxy/provider.py` (`context_pressure_ratio` / `should_warn_context_pressure`,
  LP-0MSDCLQ2W001LGWC). Add a configurable compaction trigger ratio
  (default 0.70), distinct from the 0.8 diagnostic warn ratio (unchanged).
- **Compaction at prompt assembly:** session history is a message list;
  summarization/truncation operates on it before dispatch. Composes with
  slot save/restore (compacted prompts restore cleanly under the
  persistence cap).
- **Summarizer:** short proxy-generated summary (cheap local call) injected
  at the top of the prompt; with summarizer-unavailable fallback to the
  truncate backstop.
- **Logging:** every compaction event logs session, before/after estimated
  tokens, turns summarized, turns dropped, summary length — traceability
  for quality regressions (F3 §7). Nothing is silent.
- **Rollout phases:**
  1. **Warn-only dry-run** — advisory (would-summarize/would-drop) log +
     stats for 48h; validate churn (< 1 compaction/session/hour) against
     F1/F2 distributions; **no dispatch behavior change**.
  2. **Enforcement** — gated on the quality experiment (LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ)
     passing its bar AND operator review of client-side compaction results.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1 Both modes: compacted prompt retains system prompt + very first user
  prompt verbatim + recent turns; middleware summarized (never silently
  dropped).
- AC2 Fast: est > 58,300 → compacted to ≤ 38K; backstop drop only for
  non-summarizable middle turns, logged, never system/first prompt.
- AC3 Cheap: est > 43,000 → compacted to ≤ 30K; non-compactable → remote
  with guidance (never silent remote, never near-full-slot local dispatch).
- AC4 Trigger routed through `context_pressure` machinery; compaction
  trigger ratio 0.70 configurable; 0.8 warn ratio behavior unchanged.
- AC5 All compaction events logged (session, before/after est tokens, turns
  summarized, turns dropped, summary length).
- AC6 Warn-only dry-run phase produces advisory logs + churn stats with
  zero dispatch changes; dry-run threshold validation recorded.
- AC7 Unit tests: retention invariant (first prompt kept), summary path,
  truncate backstop boundaries, turn-split prohibition, non-compactable
  routing, warn-only mode. Full suite green.
- AC8 Enforcement only after experiment (LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ) passes its
  bar AND client-side compaction review (ContextHub WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6) is
  complete; no behavior change in warn-only phase.

## Interaction analysis (from F4 §5)

- **Slot save/restore:** summary + recent turns are byte-stable → clean
  restores under the persistence cap.
- **Hard-routing-cap companion (Tier 2, LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S):** cap at
  70K/61.4K is the final bypass guard; compaction trigger fires below it so
  sessions rarely reach the cap.
- **KV-cache quantization (LP-0MSDCLQ2W001LGWC):** additive — compaction
  shrinks context length, q8_0 shrinks bytes/token; both raise decode
  headroom.

## Out of scope

- Client-side compaction UX (ContextHub owns it; see WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6).
- 150K–480K HTTP-400 cluster (LP-0MSC1BNP90017L9K).
- Changing the 0.8 diagnostic warn ratio.

## Dependencies

- Depends on LP-0MSG9PUHU0059TTZ (quality experiment) for the enforcement
  go/no-go.
- **Blocked pending:** client-side compaction results (ContextHub
  WL-0MTBOXEGR009KDP6 and completed compact-and-continue machinery) —
  operator decision 2026-08-28 to delay server-side until those are
  reviewed.
- Complementary to LP-0MTBOX45O005LD1S (Tier 2 hard cap + cheap gate).
data.title: Implement proxy-side proactive session compaction (Tier 1: truncate 58.3K / hybrid 43K)

# Feature: Core summarization compaction (fast + cheap modes)

Implement Strategy C (summarize-first) for both fast and cheap modes.

## Fast mode
- **Trigger:** est_tokens > 58,300 (= 0.70 × per-slot clamp 83,285)
- **Target:** compacted prompt ≤ 38,000 tokens
- **Retention invariant:** system prompt + very first user prompt always verbatim; recent turns retained; middle folded into summary

## Cheap mode
- **Trigger:** est_tokens > 43,000 (= 0.70 × static clamp 61,440)
- **Target:** compacted prompt ≤ 30,000 tokens
- **Retention invariant:** same as fast mode
- **Non-compactable:** route remote with guidance (never silent remote, never near-full-slot local dispatch)

## Retention invariant (both modes)
The compacted prompt MUST always contain, unchanged:
1. the system prompt
2. the **very first user prompt** (original task statement/setup)
3. the most recent turns within budget

Everything between the first prompt and the recent window is folded into a summary injected below the retained first prompt.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1 Retention invariant: system prompt + very first user prompt verbatim in all compacted outputs (unit + integration test)
- AC2 Fast trigger fires at est_tokens > 58,300; compacted output ≤ 38K tokens
- AC3 Cheap trigger fires at est_tokens > 43,000; compacted output ≤ 30K tokens
- AC4 Non-compactable cheap sessions route remote with guidance (never silent)
- AC5 Summary injected at top of prompt below retained first prompt
- AC6 Unit tests: fast mode summary path, cheap mode summary path, token budget enforcement, non-compactable routing
- AC7 Composes with slot save/restore — compacted prompts restore cleanly under the persistence cap

# Feature: Truncate backstop (both modes)

When summarization alone cannot bring the session under budget, drop oldest non-first turns as a logged backstop. This is a safety net — never the primary mechanism.

## Behavior
- Only triggers when the summary path still leaves the session over budget
- Drops oldest **whole turns** only — never split a turn
- Never drops: system prompt, first user prompt
- Every backstop event is logged (turns dropped, remaining budget)

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1 Backstop triggers only when summary path still over budget after summarization
- AC2 Whole turns dropped — never split a turn; never system/first prompt
- AC3 Every backstop event logged with turns dropped and remaining budget
- AC4 Unit tests: backstop boundaries, turn-split prohibition, first-prompt protection
data.title: Truncate backstop for both modes

# Feature: Compaction event logging

Log every compaction event with structured data for traceability and quality validation.

## Log format
Every compaction event (summary path, backstop, dry-run advisory, remote fallback) MUST log:
- Session ID
- Pre-compaction estimated tokens
- Post-compaction estimated tokens
- Number of turns summarized
- Number of turns dropped (if backstop fired)
- Summary length (tokens)
- Mode (fast/cheap)
- Dry-run flag (true/false)

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1 All compaction paths emit structured log entries with the fields above
- AC2 No silent drops — every compaction event is logged
- AC3 Unit tests: verify log emission on all compaction paths
- **Depends on:** LP-0MTGBOOJY004OWPI (core compaction)
data.title: Compaction event logging

# Feature: Warn-only dry-run mode

Deploy with advisory logging only — zero dispatch behavior change — for validation of churn rate.

## Behavior
- Config flag `compaction.dry_run: true` enables advisory mode
- In dry-run: logs what WOULD happen (would-summarize / would-drop) without changing dispatch
- Collects and logs churn stats (compactions per session per hour)
- Target validation: churn < 1 compaction/session/hour

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1 Dry-run mode flag (config): when enabled, logs advisory without dispatch change
- AC2 Churn stats collected and logged
- AC3 Unit tests: dry-run mode produces no dispatch changes; advisory logs emitted
- **Depends on:** LP-0MTGBOOJY004OWPI, LP-0MTGBOYJX006KVN8, LP-0MTGBP8DX003R5ZO
data.title: Warn-only dry-run mode

# Feature: Integration & end-to-end verification

Full integration tests verifying the complete compaction flow across fast/cheap modes, retention invariant, and all fallback paths.
